comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded Processor and GPU Product Portfolio
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD offers embedded CPUs, APUs, and GPUs, including EPYC Embedded, Ryzen Embedded V/R-Series, and Radeon Embedded products, designed for high-performance compute, networking, storage, and graphics in enterprise and automotive markets.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and MU provide embedded solutions for the automotive market, specifically mentioning infotainment. AMD states its embedded processors and GPUs support the 3D graphics performance and 4K multimedia requirements of automotive infotainment systems. MU notes that automotive memory enables connected infotainment systems with larger and higher definition displays. While both serve the same vehicle subsystem (infotainment), AMD provides the processing/graphics logic and MU provides the data storage/memory components necessary for these displays.

sentences.text: Automotive memory and storage products enable connected, advanced infotainment systems with increasingly larger and higher definition displays and support improved voice and gesture control.

Our embedded processors and GPUs are designed to support high performance compute, high-bandwidth network connectivity and security, high-performance storage requirements for enterprise and cloud infrastructure, 3D graphics performance and 4K multimedia requirements of automotive infotainment systems.

comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom provides products for factory automation, renewable energy, and automotive markets, including optocouplers, sensors, and Ethernet ICs used in EV powertrains and driver assistance systems.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures identify automotive applications for their products, specifically mentioning advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) and infotainment. AVGO lists its industrial products as being used in vehicle subsystems including those used in infotainment and ADAS. MU discusses the demand for memory and storage driven by ADAS and in-vehicle infotainment. While AVGO focuses on component types like optocouplers and sensors, and MU on memory/storage, both confirm these specific automotive subsystems as active markets for their embedded products.

sentences.text: Automotive: Advancements in autonomous driving, advanced driver-assistance systems, and in-vehicle infotainment systems continue to increase the requirements for high-performing memory and storage products, with higher reliability requirements for leading-edge products.
Automotive memory and storage products enable connected, advanced infotainment systems with increasingly larger and higher definition displays and support improved voice and gesture control.

Our industrial products are used in a diverse set of applications, spanning industrial automation, power generation and distribution systems, medical systems and equipment, defense and aerospace, and vehicle subsystems including those used in electric vehicle powertrain, infotainment and advanced driver assistance systems.

comparisons.peer_topic: x86 Ecosystem Strategy and Advisory Group
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel's core strategy relies on the x86 ecosystem, advancing it through microarchitectures focused on performance and efficiency. In 2024, the company created an advisory group to expand ecosystem compatibility, simplify software development, and identify future architectural needs.
comparisons.comparison: Intel mentions that its product offerings serve emerging fields including autonomous driving, scaling from data center to edge computing. This aligns with the broader market trend described by MU regarding the increasing requirements for memory and storage in autonomous driving and ADAS. However, Intel's disclosure focuses on its x86 ecosystem and microarchitecture strategy as the foundation for these computing capabilities, whereas MU focuses on the specific memory storage qualifications enabling those systems.

sentences.text: Automotive: Advancements in autonomous driving, advanced driver-assistance systems, and in-vehicle infotainment systems continue to increase the requirements for high-performing memory and storage products, with higher reliability requirements for leading-edge products.

Our product offerings provide end-to-end solutions, scaling from data center to network, PCs, edge computing, and the emerging fields of AI and autonomous driving, to serve an increasingly smart and connected world.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA advances its autonomous vehicle (AV) and electric vehicle (EV) strategy through the DRIVE brand, offering an AI-based hardware and software solution designed to automotive safety standards. The platform supports complex autonomous driving algorithms via neural networks and includes hardware for training and simulating these networks.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and NVDA describe the automotive market demand driven by autonomous driving and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). MU focuses on the underlying memory/storage components required for reliability in these systems, noting the qualification of specific products like LPDDR5X for cloud-connected platforms. NVDA focuses on the AI-based hardware and software platform (DRIVE brand) used to execute the complex autonomous driving algorithms, noting that traditional hand-coded approaches are insufficient for tasks like perception and planning. Both identify the shift toward complex, data-rich automotive systems as a key market driver.

sentences.text: Automotive: Advancements in autonomous driving, advanced driver-assistance systems, and in-vehicle infotainment systems continue to increase the requirements for high-performing memory and storage products, with higher reliability requirements for leading-edge products.

In 2024, we qualified our automotive LPDDR5X, UFS 3.1, and NOR flash storage solutions for a comprehensive set of cloud-connected platforms designed for power data-rich, intelligent automotive services.
We believe the advent of autonomous vehicles, or AV, and electric vehicles, or EV, is revolutionizing the transportation industry.

Therefore, we provide an AI-based hardware and software solution, designed and implemented from the ground up based on automotive safety standards, for the AV and EV market under the DRIVE brand, which we are bringing to market through our partnerships with automotive OEMs, tier-1 suppliers, and start-ups.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA leverages its AI technology leadership to deliver end-to-end automated driving and in-vehicle cockpit computing solutions under the DRIVE Hyperion brand, which includes high-performance computing hardware, sensor sets, and software platforms for autonomous driving and intelligent in-vehicle experiences.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address in-vehicle infotainment and cockpit computing as part of the automotive market. MU notes that automotive memory products enable connected infotainment systems with larger displays and improved control interfaces. NVDA provides a more comprehensive view of the cockpit, offering end-to-end solutions under the DRIVE Hyperion brand that include intelligent in-vehicle experiences alongside automated driving capabilities. While MU highlights the memory content enablement, NVDA highlights the computing architecture that powers these experiences.

sentences.text: Automotive memory and storage products enable connected, advanced infotainment systems with increasingly larger and higher definition displays and support improved voice and gesture control.
Automotive market is comprised of platform solutions for automated driving and in-vehicle cockpit computing.

DRIVE Hyperion consists of the high-performance, energy efficient DRIVE AGX computing hardware, a reference sensor set that supports full self-driving capability as well as an open, modular DRIVE software platform for autonomous driving, mapping, and parking services, and intelligent in-vehicle experiences.

comparisons.peer_summary: High-performance computing technologies are improving advanced driver assistance and automated driving features, with estimates suggesting 39% of new light-duty vehicles sold in 2027 will have Level 2 or higher autonomy.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and QCOM discuss the growth of autonomous driving features and the technological requirements driving this trend. MU highlights that advancements in autonomous driving and ADAS increase requirements for high-performing and reliable memory/storage. QCOM similarly notes that high-performance, low-power computing technologies with added security and safety are improving ADAS and automated driving features. QCOM provides specific market data estimating a rise in Level 2+ autonomy adoption, while MU focuses on the product qualification outcomes (LPDDR5X, NOR flash) supporting these vehicle tiers.

sentences.text: Automotive: Advancements in autonomous driving, advanced driver-assistance systems, and in-vehicle infotainment systems continue to increase the requirements for high-performing memory and storage products, with higher reliability requirements for leading-edge products.
Adoption of Level 2+ advanced driver-assistance systems capabilities continue to gain momentum, further expanding content per vehicle.

In addition, high-performance, low-power computing technologies, with added security and safety required for automotive products, are being used to improve vehicles with advanced driver assistance and automated driving features that we expect to scale across vehicle tiers and continue the progression toward higher levels of autonomy, safety and convenience.

Analysts estimate that 39% of new light duty vehicles sold globally in 2027 will have Level 2 (i.e., partial driving automation) or higher autonomy, compared to an estimated 20% of new light duty vehicles sold globally in 2024 (TechInsights, September 2024).

comparisons.peer_summary: The company is driving digital transformation in automotive via Snapdragon Digital Chassis platforms for connectivity and ADAS/AD, and in IoT across consumer, edge networking, and industrial applications such as PCs, tablets, and logistics.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the integration of automotive solutions into broader connectivity and ecosystem strategies. MU details how its embedded business unit qualifies memory solutions for cloud-connected platforms. QCOM describes its Snapdragon Digital Chassis platform, which connects the car to the environment and the cloud, encompassing connectivity, digital cockpit, and ADAS. Both recognize the trend of vehicles becoming data-rich and connected entities, though MU focuses on the storage component and QCOM on the connectivity/computing platform.

sentences.text: In 2024, we qualified our automotive LPDDR5X, UFS 3.1, and NOR flash storage solutions for a comprehensive set of cloud-connected platforms designed for power data-rich, intelligent automotive services.

In automotive, our Snapdragon® Digital Chassis™ platforms, including connectivity, digital cockpit and advanced driver assistance and automated driving (ADAS/AD), are helping to connect the car to its environment and the cloud, creating unique in-cabin experiences and enabling a comprehensive assisted and automated driving solution.
